Subject: Preflight — sample traffic smoke run & evidence deliverables

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the quick onboarding call yesterday. To finish our internal readiness review we need to run a short sample-traffic smoke test (5–10 minutes) against the private deployment and collect a few pieces of evidence for our security/compliance team. Can you confirm who on Redwood’s side will own the run and whether you can provide a short checklist of what you’ll collect?

Specifically we need:
- a short network diagram that includes egress IPs and ports (for our firewall team)
- confirmation of KMS keyholder/account and whether wrap/unwrap operations will be performed by us or Redwood
- a pcap of a representative 5–10 minute session (we can redact payloads)
- timestamps and runbook steps so our auditors can map activity to logs

Attached: healthsync-network-diagram-v2.pdf (internal diagram)

Can we target Monday (Oct 11) 15:00 PT for the run? That gives our ops folks time to carve a maintenance window.

Thanks,
Lena

Lena / team —

Quick technical confirmation from network/KMS side:

- Egress IPs (public): 34.201.12.45, 34.201.12.46, 34.201.12.47 (these are NATed EIPs from our dedicated pool).
- Ports: outbound TCP 443, 5222 (for telemetry), and ephemeral 32768–32775 for backend health checks.
- CSV attached: egress-allowlist.csv

KMS flow (short):
- HealthSync creates customer-managed key in their KMS and stores a wrapped DEK (data encryption key) in HealthSync’s key vault.
- Redwood will request the wrapped DEK via an authenticated key-retrieval API; unwrap is performed in HealthSync’s KMS. Redwood will never see plaintext DEK.
- IAM notes: Redwood’s runner service account needs kms:getWrappedKey and kms:listKeys on the delegated key alias. We will provide an example IAM policy in the Drive folder.

Ben — I added a couple of minor adjustments to the runbook (command timeouts + extra header logging).

—Karthik
